source.name: Blackstone Private Credit Fund Form 10-Q, quarter ended June 30, 2026 (filed Aug 12, 2026)

summary.headline: BCRED is a non-traded business development company that lends directly to private companies, mostly through first lien, floating-rate loans. Investors buy shares at a monthly NAV, and the fund buys shares back through quarterly tender offers.

thisQuarter: Investors asked to sell back more shares than the quarterly limit allowed, so requests were filled pro rata. The fund bought back 5.0% of shares ($2.20B at $23.65).
In the first quarter it bought back 7.0% of shares ($3.23B at $24.19), more than the 5% quarterly level.

Fifteen issuers, across 25 loans, were on non-accrual status, up from nine issuers across 16 loans at year-end. Non-accrual is the filing's term for loans where there is reasonable doubt that principal or interest will be collected in full.

howItWorks.title: How this fund works
paragraphs: The fund lends to private companies. 91% of its investments are first lien loans, which hold the most senior claim on a borrower's assets, and 99.8% of its performing loans carry a floating rate that moves with market rates.
The share price (net asset value) is set every month.
At the board's discretion, the fund may buy back up to 5% of its shares each quarter through tender offers, at that quarter's NAV. Shares held for less than a year are bought back at 98% of NAV.
When requests exceed the limit they are filled pro rata, as happened this quarter. The board can amend or suspend the program, and bought back more than 5% in the first quarter.

website.text: BCRED's website describes its focus as floating-rate, senior secured loans to large, performing companies.
